answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a scarce token in a public bond before it may post offers or claim rewards. A wharf operator, for example, can slash that bond when a verified task is fraudulent, while honest agents recover it after a dispute window. Creating a thousand identities then requires a thousand separate bonds, each exposed to loss; recycling one identity’s echo cannot multiply its stake. At the zenith of an attack, capital locked across those accounts is costly and unavailable for other uses.
